body:
Good Wednesday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a hard one: a 33-year-old Oildale woman who told 23ABC she was set on fire at a homeless encampment has died, and her family is still waiting on answers from the coroner. It's going to be a hot one — a high near 100° — with moderate air quality and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came just after 2 a.m., when crews were sent to a vehicle-versus-pedestrian crash on southbound Highway 99 just north of Lerdo Highway. A vehicle was reported facing the wrong way in the freeway, and as units responded, dispatchers learned three vehicles were involved and two people were hurt — one of them a pedestrian who was struck. That upgraded the call to a rescue. The pedestrian was reported down in the number one lane and possibly in grave condition, and a second unit passing the scene about half a mile into the southbound lanes reported several vehicles involved.

Elsewhere in east Kern County, a single vehicle landed on its roof on Highway 14, and a Mercy Air helicopter was placed on standby. Crews found one patient who was not pinned but had limited access, so they began an extrication; the air ambulance was later stood down. Fire crews also answered smoke at the back of a commercial building in the 2100 block of Niles Street — a structure that had burned before — and found smoke at the rear on arrival.

A car and a semi collided near East Bear Mountain Boulevard, with all occupants reported out of the vehicles, the car blocking traffic and one patient transported. On southbound Highway 99 south of Highway 166, a semi went into a guardrail with heavy smoke visible, hung up on the rail for about 50 feet; Caltrans was asked to respond to the road hazard. The rest of the log was the usual overnight mix: a domestic disturbance on Gold Dust Drive, a semi with brakes on fire northbound on Interstate 5 north of the Grapevine whose driver pulled into the scales, an animal bite on East Roberts Lane, and a handful of medical aids, alarms and welfare checks across the county.

## Today's weather

It's currently 75° at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 100° this afternoon and a low around 70° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires reported. Air quality sits at 71 on the index — moderate — so if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a day to keep an eye on how you're feeling during the hottest hours. Otherwise, expect a classic early-October valley scorcher: hot, dry and still. Drink more water than you think you need, and don't leave anyone in a parked car.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Frances Lopez, the 33-year-old woman who told the station last week she was set on fire at a homeless encampment in Oildale, has died.** Lopez spent nearly two months in a Fresno burn unit recovering from burns covering more than 30% of her body, undergoing multiple surgeries and needing daily care after she left the hospital. Her husband, Steven, said the couple had been together 13 years and were raising two daughters; her grandparents visited every weekend while she was treated. The Kern County Sheriff's Office told 23ABC it is awaiting the coroner's report to determine her cause of death, and the family says a full autopsy could take about three weeks. Her loved ones believe an infection, possibly sepsis, related to her injuries may have played a role, but that has not been confirmed.

**According to KGET 17, State Sen. Ben Allen brought his campaign for California's insurance commissioner to Bakersfield, telling the station the Central Valley is "vital" and needs to be part of the conversation.** Allen, an attorney who represents parts of the Los Angeles coast, is running in November against former San Francisco supervisor and attorney Jane Kim. The commissioner's office regulates insurance rates, licenses companies and agents, investigates fraud and enforces consumer protection laws — all subjects that land squarely on Kern County homeowners, drivers and farmers. 23ABC also sat down with both candidates; Kim told the station she wants the state to take a bigger stake in the insurance market, pitching a public nonprofit disaster insurance program for every California homeowner.

**23ABC reports that Cal State Bakersfield has hired Andy Fiske, most recently of Sacramento State, as its new director of athletics — stepping into one of the most legally turbulent chapters in the department's recent history.** Two former softball players have sued CSUB and a former assistant coach alleging harassment; former Athletic Director Kyle Conder filed a separate suit alleging retaliation and defamation, claims the university denies; and former assistant basketball coach Kevin Mays pleaded no contest to pimping, possession of child pornography and drug possession while armed, and was sentenced to four years in prison. At a press conference, Fiske said challenges should be faced directly and mistakes acknowledged and learned from, and that his first 90 to 100 days will focus on listening. Asked what accountability athletes should see from him, he pointed to reporting structures he has used at previous institutions and said he'd find out whether similar avenues exist here. KGET 17 also covered the hire, noting the university's aim to change the culture of the program.

**KGET 17 reports that the death of a 14-year-old Oildale girl has sparked an outpouring of community support.** That's the extent of what we can tell you from the headline alone this morning; we'll bring you more as details are confirmed.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a CHP crackdown on Interstate 5 ended with two vehicles impounded and multiple citations issued to trucks.** Commercial enforcement sweeps like this one target equipment, weight and safety violations on one of the busiest freight corridors in the state — the kind of enforcement that matters in a county where I-5 traffic and truck safety are a daily concern for everyone sharing the road.

## Something good

CSUB has hired Andy Fiske as its new athletic director, and the university is framing the move as a fresh chapter for Bakersfield's hometown university and its student-athletes. It's a hard moment to step into, and Fiske's stated first move — listening — is the right one. Here's hoping the Roadrunners get the steady, accountable leadership they deserve, on the field and off.

## Coming up this week

City business gets moving early today. The Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 this morning, followed by a special Police Civil Service Commission meeting at 8:45, and the City Council takes up Meeting 330 at 3:30 this afternoon. On Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon. Friday brings the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee at noon — a good room for anyone who cares about the litter, blight and cleanup work that shapes how our neighborhoods look.

Next week opens with a pair of Monday meetings: a Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee session at noon and the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m. On Tuesday, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon — the place to be if you have thoughts on bike lanes, crosswalks or how traffic moves through town.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch ahead: the NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour lands Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. Later in the month, United We Dance brings an all-night festival energy to the Fox on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour stops in October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour closes out the run on October 18. Season passes for Cults & Classics 2026–2027 are also on sale now.

Have a good Wednesday, and stay cool out there.

top.title: Woman who said she was set on fire at Oildale homeless encampment dies months after suffering severe burns
